segments.t: At half past two—thirty minutes before the City Hall heritage visit—Qing, Teacher Song, and Chen put the finishing touches on the sunlit tables inside Room Nine. Listen first.
四块白亚麻桌布熨得平平的，每张桌子围三把折叠椅。
小晴，你看每个小玻璃花瓶里插一片绿叶多好看。
十分钟以前，我已经把木头欢迎牌挂到大门外了。
老陈，梧桐巷上有人停下来看牌子吗？
有三位邻居把每个字都读完了，还问茶壶几点烧开！
听我弹一下钢琴上接到第二十八小节的过渡段……
每一个音符都温暖又清脆——特别是中央瑞音！
把对着院子的两扇拱窗敞开吧，让琴声飘出去。
看我的谱架：第一页是周经理姑姑的黑墨水，第二页是我的。
隔了三十年，连成同一首圆舞曲。
我的手表两点四十五了。周经理去哪儿了？
正在镜子前面练习欢迎词呢——我们快去救他吧！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
四块白亚麻桌布熨得平平的，每张桌子围三把折叠椅。

'Four white linen tablecloths ironed nice and flat, with three folding chairs around each table.' Doubling the word for "flat" makes the freshly ironed linen sound extra neat and smooth—a warm spoken Mandarin touch.
小晴，你看每个小玻璃花瓶里插一片绿叶多好看。
'Look how pretty a single green leaf looks in each small glass vase, Qing.' "Vase" in Mandarin simply joins "flower" and "bottle", while "pretty" literally says "good-to-look-at".
十分钟以前，我已经把木头欢迎牌挂到大门外了。
'I hung the wooden welcome sign outside the front gate ten minutes ago.' In Mandarin, "ten minutes ago" sits right at the opening of the sentence, setting the clock before describing what Chen did.
老陈，梧桐巷上有人停下来看牌子吗？
'Did anyone on Wutong Lane stop to read the sign, Chen?' Mandarin links "stop down" directly to "read the sign" with no extra linker needed where English puts "to".
有三位邻居把每个字都读完了，还问茶壶几点烧开！

'Three neighbours read every single word and asked what time the tea kettle boils!' Chen picks the respectful counter for people rather than the plain everyday one, showing quiet fondness for the street regulars.
听我弹一下钢琴上接到第二十八小节的过渡段……

'Listen while I play the transition into bar twenty-eight on the piano...' Mandarin adds "one quick stroke" right after "play" to make Teacher Song sound relaxed and modest—"let me just play a quick bit".
每一个音符都温暖又清脆——特别是中央瑞音！
'Every single note rings warm and clear—especially middle D!' Mandarin builds "musical note" from "sound" plus "symbol", and names "middle D" after the solfege syllable "Re".
把对着院子的两扇拱窗敞开吧，让琴声飘出去。

'Leave the two arched courtyard windows wide open so the piano music floats outside.' In Mandarin, doors and windows take their own classic counter, which originally pictured one swinging panel of a bamboo gate.
看我的谱架：第一页是周经理姑姑的黑墨水，第二页是我的。

'Look at my music stand: Manager Zhou's aunt's black ink on page one, mine on page two.' At the very end, Mandarin adds a tiny word onto "I" to turn "my" into standalone "mine" without repeating "ink".
隔了三十年，连成同一首圆舞曲。
'Thirty years apart, joined into one continuous waltz.' In Mandarin, songs and poems share an elegant counter that literally meant "head", since ancient verses were listed by their opening lines.
我的手表两点四十五了。周经理去哪儿了？
'Quarter to three on my watch. Where did Manager Zhou go?' "Wristwatch" literally says "hand-meter", setting a watch on your wrist apart from a clock on the wall.
正在镜子前面练习欢迎词呢——我们快去救他吧！

'Practising his welcome speech in front of the mirror—let's go rescue him!' Pairing "right-at" in front with that friendly spoken tag near the middle drops us right into the ongoing action, like English "-ing".
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.

Room Nine sparkles in the afternoon sun, neighbours are already curious at the gate, and three o'clock is fifteen minutes away. See you next time.
下次见！
